audit.why: 7.5/10 at 49.76% over 822 games is fair, and the shipped chart (Rumble 4 / Skill 3) matches the story the prose tells — he owns 2-3 and both item stages, you get 4-5 and a coin-flip 6. Full and content agree row for row, and the mirror recorded no point-2 correction, so the two directions do not conflict.

Spike order holds. The Equalizer is 130/105/80 against All Out's 120/100/80 — near-parity, which is why level 6 is correctly written as a coin flip decided by heat rather than by ultimate uptime. The mirror already fixed the same three spikes from Rumble's side (Path Maker at 14s, the wall on All Out, the pull on two Q stacks) and this side now states them identically.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (1) 'W-charge for the damage resistance and unstoppable' — Riot's text for Path Maker is 'charges up, taking reduced damage'; the damage reduction is real, the unstoppable is not in the kit. (2) Overheat is described backwards, twice: 'overheat his Flamespitter to silence-burn you' and 'before he learns to overheat on my engage'. Junkyard Titan's Overheat is Rumble's OWN penalty — at 100% Heat he 'starts Overheating ... but making him unable to cast spells'. He is the one who gets silenced, and that is your window, not his. (3) 'Q3 knock-up' three times — Ntofo Strikes slows and pulls at two stacks; Path Maker is the stun.
audit.why: The Overheat reversal turns the single best commit window in the lane into a reason to back off. A player reading this waits out exactly the moment they should be walking in.
audit.corrected: At 100% Heat Rumble cannot cast spells at all — commit into that. Below it, Danger Zone (50% Heat) is what empowers his basics. Flamespitter is 10/9/8/7/6s at 600 range; Scrap Shield 6s; Electro Harpoon holds two charges at 850 range on a 0.5s cast cooldown and reduces your magic resist as well as slowing. Path Maker's charge reduces damage taken and stuns on release.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's headline advice is 'build MR' and its TL;DR calls his damage a '%HP DoT'. Flamespitter is flat magic damage in Riot's text with no percent-health component and no percentHealth flag — and nothing warned that Electro Harpoon reduces the magic resist you just bought, two charges at a time.
audit.why: Calling flat magic damage percent-health changes what a player builds, and MR shred is the reason MR alone is not the whole answer here.
audit.corrected: TL;DR now says magic DoT; the MR-shred on Electro Harpoon is stated in mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the first person ('chip me at level 1', 'my window', 'I can't bet on the very late 1v1').
audit.why: The site's voice is second person; a first-person block reads as a different author mid-page.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person inside the length band, with the Overheat and MR-shred corrections folded in.

edits.after: His magic DoT hurts — build MR, dodge his R. K'Sante wins the Scrap Shield cooldown windows.

edits.before: Rumble has no mana, so his Flamespitter is always available to chip me at level 1 — I farm and don't walk into the cone for free. My Q out-ranges nothing he has, but his early DPS can't out-trade my bulk if I pick the window. By level 3 I have my full kit: W-charge for the damage resistance and unstoppable, push through his Flamespitter, and Q3 to knock him up and pull him in. The key is committing W while his heat bar is low — if he's overheated and silence-burning, I eat far more than I deal.
edits.after: Rumble has no mana, so Flamespitter is always available to chip you at level 1 — farm and don't stand in the cone for free. His early DPS still can't out-trade your bulk if you pick the window. By level 3 you have the full kit: charge Path Maker for the damage reduction, push through the burn, stun him on the release, and pull him back with your second Q stack. Watch his heat bar — at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all, and that is the window you commit into.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my window. I trade around his Flamespitter cooldown: W-charge to negate his burn DPS, Q3 the knock-up, and my tank stats bank a small lead before he learns to overheat on my engage. Dodge his E harpoon — if it slows me I can't reach him with my short W and Q, and he just kites my whole cooldown pattern. At 6 it's a genuine coin flip: All Out gives me a duelist 1v1, but it strips my bulk right when his Equalizer can melt a squishier me, so I only ult when his ult and overheat are both down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your window. Trade around Flamespitter's 10s cooldown: charge Path Maker to blunt the burn, pull him in with your second Q, and let your tank stats bank a small lead. Dodge Electro Harpoon — he carries two charges at 850 range and each one shreds your magic resist as well as slowing you out of your own reach. At 6 it's a genuine coin flip: All Out gives you the 1v1 but strips your resists right when The Equalizer can melt a squishier you, so ult only once his R is spent.

edits.before: This is where Rumble takes it back. My armor stacking does literally nothing against his magic damage, so a full-build Rumble out-burns me with overheated Flamespitter and Equalizer zoning the second my windows close. I can't bet on the very late 1v1 here — he's a scaler against my profile. My job is to have banked my Level 3-to-first-item leads, then pivot to teamfights where my R peels his carries and my W eats his ult damage for the team, instead of trying to solo-duel a champion my whole defensive kit is blank against.
edits.after: This is where Rumble takes it back. Armour stacking does literally nothing against his magic damage, and every Electro Harpoon shreds the magic resist you did buy, so a full-build Rumble out-burns you the second your windows close. Don't bet on the very late 1v1 — he scales against your profile. Bank your Level 3-to-first-item leads, then pivot to teamfights where your R peels his carries and Path Maker's charge soaks the Equalizer line, instead of solo-duelling a champion your defences are blank against.

notes: The packet's suspectName ('Drop Equalizer' in wants.foe[2]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the ability is The Equalizer and the sentence just drops the article. The real defect was that Overheat was described as something Rumble does TO you, when Riot's passive text says it leaves HIM unable to cast. One field I could not fix: dontsFull[1].t reads 'Stack pure HP vs %damage', which repeats the percent-health error, but at 24 characters it falls under the applier's 25-character skip threshold, so it needs a manual edit. I also did not write the flagged 'dash-denied' interaction (Scrap Shield / The Equalizer denying your dashes) — neither Riot description contains any grounding or dash-stopping clause, and the mirror audit's notes record the same class of flag misfire on this pairing.
